title: The Day of the LORD Draws Near
summary_text: The LORD's word through Zephaniah announces a sweeping destruction of life on earth. He will strike Judah and Jerusalem, removing idols, false worship, and those who no longer seek Him. He describes His coming day as a prepared sacrifice and promises to punish rulers, violent people, and those who assume He will never act. The Day of the LORD approaches with war, darkness, and wrath because people have sinned against Him. Their wealth will offer no escape from His consuming judgment.
key_points: The LORD announces destruction across the earth and judgment on Judah's idols and false worship.
The LORD has prepared a sacrifice and will punish rulers and those practicing violence and deceit.
Jerusalem's commerce and wealth will be lost, and people who think the LORD does nothing will face punishment.
The coming day brings war and wrath because of sin, and silver and gold cannot save anyone.

title: Seek the LORD Before Judgment Comes
summary_text: The nation is told to gather before the LORD's anger arrives, and the humble are urged to seek righteousness and humility in hope of shelter. The LORD's word announces ruin for the Philistine coast, which Judah's remnant will later possess. Moab and Ammon will become wastelands because of their proud insults against His people. Nations will worship the LORD as He removes the gods' strength. Cush also faces death, and proud Nineveh will become a deserted home for animals.
key_points: The humble must seek the LORD, righteousness, and humility before His anger comes.
The LORD's word condemns the Philistine coast, which will become pasture for Judah's remnant.
Moab and Ammon face ruin for pride and insults, while peoples everywhere will worship the LORD.
Cush faces the LORD's sword, and Nineveh's proud security will end in desolation among wild animals.

title: The LORD Restores and Rejoices over Jerusalem
summary_text: Jerusalem refuses correction while its rulers, prophets, and priests corrupt justice and law, though the LORD remains righteous within it. He announces judgment on gathered nations, then promises pure speech so peoples can call on Him together. He will remove pride from His holy mountain and leave a humble, truthful remnant whose transgressions no longer bring shame. Jerusalem is called to rejoice because the LORD, its King, has removed punishment and is mighty to save. He will rejoice over His people, gather the scattered, and replace their disgrace with honor.
key_points: Jerusalem's rulers, prophets, and priests act corruptly, but the LORD remains righteous and just.
After announcing judgment, the LORD promises that peoples will call on Him together and bring an offering.
God will remove pride from His holy mountain and leave a humble remnant without shame for past transgressions.
Jerusalem can rejoice because the LORD is among His people, mighty to save and rejoicing over them.
The LORD will gather scattered and afflicted people and turn their disgrace into honor.
